bullets: Internal save schema cleanup. Equipment now lives in one place (the owned-equipment ledger that the picker reads) instead of being mirrored under inventory; the journal is permanent apartment furniture, not an inventory line item. Bottling bucket and auto-siphon now seed for fresh careers since the bottling flow has always assumed both — they used to be implicitly granted, now they're real items in your inventory from day one.

Dashboard's sink-tap is now recipe-aware. The starter recipe slot used to be hardcoded; with one recipe unlocked the behavior is identical, but adding a second recipe to the journal (next on the build sequence) won't require a code change.
Old saves auto-migrate on load. If you started a career before this update, the migration tops up any missing starter equipment without touching your cash, skills, brews-in-flight, or shop progress.

Build pipeline back on Godot 4.6.2 with min Android 7.0 (API 24). The v0.2.88 force-close was tracked down to the in-app Java overlay (Firebase init, install handler) — its source files were laid out for the older Godot 4.3 build template, so Godot 4.6's gradle build never compiled them, and Android force-closed at launch trying to instantiate a class that wasn't in the APK. Overlay relocated to the layout the new build expects; locally verified the app boots past startup on a clean install.
Reverted v0.2.88. That build wouldn't launch on phones — restoring the v0.2.86 baseline (Godot 4.3 build pipeline, original picker labels) while we investigate the Godot 4.6 + Android startup crash.
Every brewing-day step is now a real interactive close-up — no more placeholder buttons. Tap stations, work the equipment, the outcome reflects what you did.

Pour LME: stove with kettle on a burner, wooden spoon in front, LME tin to the right. Tap the dial to turn the burner off (flame disappears), tap the spoon to start stirring (animated stir + swirl in the kettle), tap the LME tin to pour (visible brown stream, tin empties, water turns wort-brown). Order still matters — burner-off → stir → pour for ideal. Wrong order = mild glob, scorch, or full catastrophic scorch.

Boil with hops: real-time mini-game. Kettle boiling on the stove with brown wort + bubbles + foam. Three hop bags on the counter glow in their drop windows (60-min bittering, 15-min flavor, 0-min aroma). Tap each during its window to drop it in (animated bag falling into the kettle). Boil-over event fires mid-boil — foam climbs and a BOIL OVER warning shows; tap the dial to lower heat (HIGH→MED→LOW) before time runs out. At the end, tap the dial to OFF for flameout.

Cool wort: kettle in a sink basin viewed cross-section. Faucet hangs above (tap to start cold water flow — visible water in the basin and a stream from the spout). Three ice bags on a side shelf (tap to drop one in — instant temp drop + ice cube animation). Wooden spoon (press-and-hold to stir — surface swirls + cooling rate boost). Thermometer on the right shows wort temp dropping from 210°F to the 70°F target band. Auto-resolves at target.

Transfer + pitch: kettle on the left, fermenter bucket on the right, auto-siphon arching between them. Funnel and yeast packet on the counter. Tap the funnel to sanitize first (improves outcome). Tap the siphon tube to start the transfer (animated wort level dropping in the kettle, rising in the fermenter; siphon tube shows the brown wort flowing through). After transfer the yeast packet glows — tap to pitch (yeast cloud appears on the wort surface).
Heat (added last commit): stove + dial + flame + steam + bubbles + hold-target meter — already real.
All sim tests still pass — internal field contracts (_heat, _selected_path, _option_toggles, etc.) preserved; the interactive UI just drives them via taps now.

Heat the kettle is a real close-up mini-game now: stove + kettle on burner cross-section, dial control with OFF/LOW/MED/HIGH, vertical thermometer with a highlighted target band at 160-170°F, hold-the-target meter at the top. Tap the dial to cycle settings; flame size scales with the position. Steam rises as the water heats; bubbles when boiling. Hold the temp in the band for 3 seconds to commit. Scorch risk if you push past 200°F.

Removed wizard chrome from the remaining mini-games (pour LME, boil with hops, cool wort, transfer + pitch). They no longer show "Step N of M" titles, instruction text, multi-radio button stacks, or optional-checkbox groups. Each shows a dark close-up backdrop with a single primary action button. The underlying outcome logic is unchanged so the existing tests still pass; richer interactive close-ups for these steps land next.

Pour LME got real hotspots: stove dial / spoon / LME tin laid out as three tap targets on the close-up. Order still matters (burner-off then stir then pour for an ideal result, scorch otherwise) — same logic, no wizard form.

Killed the wizard. There's no more step-by-step "Step 2 of 7 · Heat the water" wrapper after fill kettle. Each station tap mounts ONE mini-game directly based on the active brew's current step, then returns you to the apartment when it's done.

Tap the SINK with no brew + the kettle in inventory → starts a brew + opens fill kettle. Tap the STOVE with a filled kettle in flight → opens the heat mini-game (or pour LME / boil with hops, depending on which step is next). Tap the BOTTLING TABLE → opens transfer + pitch. Tap a station whose step isn't current → silent ignore.

Sanitize is auto-completed when you start a brew (default care factor) so the player doesn't sit through a wizard panel for a step that's just "wipe down the gear" — re-add a real sanitize mini-game later if it becomes a meaningful interaction.
When all brewing-day steps are done, the brew advances to fermenting on its own. Tap the closet to check the fermenter.

Cabinet knobs no longer centered horizontally — they now sit on the swing side of each door (alternating left/right so adjacent doors look like hinge-pairs). Sink-base double-door knobs moved BELOW the basin recess so they're visible (a real sink-base door is shorter than the adjacent cabinet doors for exactly this reason).

Active-brews HUD: a sidebar list on the left side of the apartment shows every brew currently in flight with its name and current stage (Brew day / Fermenting N/M / Conditioning N/M). Tap a brew card to open its details panel.

Brew details panel: shows ingredient list with green checks (have it) or red x (missing), plus the full step list — sanitize, fill kettle, heat, add malt, boil with hops, cool wort, transfer + pitch, ferment, bottle, condition, taste — with completion checks and care-factor scores per finished step.

Fill kettle is a true close-up now. Distinct view from the apartment: kettle takes the lower half of the screen, faucet hangs above. Cross-section silhouette so you can see water level rising INSIDE the pot through the cutaway side wall. Tap the lever handle on the faucet to toggle on/off.

Liquid physics: surface waves are a sum-of-sines (5 Hz + 7.3 Hz with phase shift), amplitude scales with how full the kettle is. After the faucet shuts off, the slosh decays toward stillness over ~1 second. Splash particles spawn at the impact point while pouring — small drops drift outward and fall under gravity, fading as they age.
Removed the gold target band from the kettle — eyeballing the level is part of the game; you don't have any aim guides yet.

Apartment layout reorganized: front door at the far left (cx 120), bottling table (with shelf + journal + calendar above) at cx 480, kitchen counter + sink + stove at 600-1020, bed UNDER the window at cx 1200, closet at the far right at cx 1500. Front door and closet are now at opposite ends of the apartment so they're not adjacent.
Window sits directly above the bed — bedroom layout. Headboard tower at the left end of the bed reaches up under the window without overlapping it.
Calendar moved BELOW the bookshelf instead of above. Stack on the bottling-table wall is now: shelf with journal → calendar → bottling table on the floor. Same x for all three.

Lower cabinet door knobs moved to near the top of the door (3" below the counter seam), where real base-cabinet knobs sit. They were rendering at the center of the door, which read as buttons-on-a-door instead of knobs.
Panorama widened to 1620 px to fit the bed + closet on the right end. Pan camera further right to see the closet.

Fixed: existing saves had no equipment in inventory because the v1 → equipment migration didn't seed it. Tapping the sink showed an empty picker. Save reseed now backfills the equipment dict (kettle, fermenter, bottling bucket, capper, auto-siphon) and the journal flag for any pre-equipment careers.

Added a real apartment front door on the far left wall — heavier wood casing, painted-deep slab, single tall inset panel with a 4-pane window in the upper portion, deadbolt above the knob, and a doormat on the floor in front. Visually distinct from the closet so it's obvious which is which. Tapping it does nothing yet — deliveries / bar / festival hooks land later.

Apartment panorama widened to 1560 px and stations shifted: front door (cx 120) → closet (264) → bottling table (480) → sink (720) → stove (960) → window (1200) → bed (1440). Pan further to see everything.

HUD stripped to just "Day N" and the Phone icon. Gone: the morning-summary line, the money-and-bottles chip, the bottom action prompt ("Tap the kettle to start a brew"), the Rest button, and the Dev Reset button.

Phone home now shows your bank balance in big gold type with bottle count below — that's the screen the player checks to know what to spend, and it's where they shop. Apps grid shows Messages, Shop, and a new Settings tile.
Settings app houses the changelog scroll and the Reset Save button (with the confirmation dialog). Version label moved into the Settings header.
Rest is now bed-only — tap the bed on the right side of the apartment to advance the day.

Cabinet bugs fixed. The right-of-sink lower cabinet was rendering as ONE huge 132-px-wide door because the door-count math used round() instead of ceil() — now it correctly subdivides into two doors. Same fix applies to the right-side upper cabinets.

Region-boundary seams between the sink-base unit and the adjacent cabinets are now drawn explicitly. They were missing on the upper cabinets, which made the over-sink door visually blend with its neighbors and look narrower than the sink-base double-door below it. They now line up.
Wall clock moved off the bottling-table wall (where it was overlapping the new bookshelf) onto the bare wall between the stove/hood and the window. Pan right from the sink to see it.
Wall calendar moved up to the top of the wall above the bottling-table shelf, so the shelf, journal, and calendar can coexist on the same wall without overlapping.

Added a bed on the right side of the apartment. Tap it to advance the day — same effect as the HUD Rest button, but you act on the world instead of a chrome icon. Apartment panorama widened to 1440 px to fit the bed; pan camera right to see it.
Range hood shrunk: 18" → 12" tall, mounted 30" above the cooktop instead of 24". Reads more like a slim apartment hood, less like a giant chimney.

Sink-base cabinet knobs moved to the middle of the door (was near the top, hugging the counter seam). The over-sink wall cabinet is now a single 24" door — same width as the sink-base double-door below — so upper and lower cabinetry line up. Adjacent wall cabinets stay at 18" doors.
Cleaned up the cabinet-door layout logic to use a shared region helper. No more duplicate knobs near the sink-base seams.

Brewing journal moved off the bottling table onto a small wall shelf above it. The notebook stands upright on the shelf showing its spine (forest-green leather with brass-trim bands and a title plate). Tap the journal as before to open the journal scene.

Sink-base cabinet redrawn as a real double-door — two narrow doors directly under the basin, knobs on the inner edges so the doors swing outward from the center seam. Adjacent cabinets keep their standard 24" doors with knobs on the seam edges.

The brewing journal is now a physical green leather notebook sitting on the bottling table. Tap it to read entries, log sessions, and (eventually) flip through discovered recipes. The HUD Journal button is gone; the journal travels with you in the apartment, not in a menu.

Inventory now tracks owned equipment (kettle, fermenter, bottling bucket, capper, auto-siphon) alongside ingredients. A new station-picker modal opens when you tap the sink with no brew in progress: it lists which of your equipment fits there. Pick the kettle to start a fresh brew. Same picker pattern will roll out to the stove and bottling table as those mini-games graphify.
EquipmentDefs registers each piece with its display name, hint, and which stations it's compatible with — the source of truth the picker reads from.

Faucet redrawn as a proper counter-mounted gooseneck. There's a brass base flange on the counter, a vertical riser, the gooseneck arches forward over the basin, and a short downturn-spout points into the kettle. A side-lever handle pivots when you toggle it on/off. No more floating-faucet-with-no-mount.

Kettle sits INSIDE the sink basin during fill. Bottom of the kettle is dropped below counter level so the basin rim wraps around it; reads like a stockpot in a sink, not a stockpot on a counter beside a hole.
Clock moved off the cabinet face. The kitchen clock now hangs on the bare wall above the bottling table; the wall calendar moved to the bare wall between the upper cabinets and the window.

Home view no longer auto-places a kettle on the counter. The room is empty by default — equipment will come from inventory when you tap a station (kettle into the sink, fermenter into the closet, etc.). The fill-kettle scene still places the kettle for now; full inventory-driven placement lands next.

Adopted a real-world scale rule: 4 pixels = 1 inch (48 px = 1 foot). Every wall object, piece of furniture, and equipment is sized against this rule so a 30" door, a 36" counter, a 12" stockpot, and a 12" wall clock are all consistent with each other. If something looks wrong, the fix is to size it in inches × 4, not eyeball it.

Closet door re-proportioned to a real 30"×80" interior door (was overly tall and narrow). Two stacked inset panels, brass knob at waist height. Stove shrunk to 30"×36" (was a giant 200×165). Window re-sized to 36"×48" with sill above counter, mullions in a + cross.

New decor on the kitchen wall: a 12" wall clock above the sink, a paper wall calendar (red header, date grid) between the closet and the bottling table, two banks of upper cabinets above the splashback, a 30"×18" range hood mounted 24" above the stove cooktop with vent slats and a drop shadow.

Sink got a real basin: stainless rim with a recessed bowl and a drain in the middle. The kettle no longer auto-parks IN the sink — it sits to the right of the basin on the counter (the rest spot). When you start brewing, fill_kettle moves it over the basin under the faucet.
Bottling table redrawn at 60"×30" with a proper apron under the top and square legs inset 4" from each end (no more squashed parallelogram look). Baseboard runs along the visible wall gaps.

Kettle and faucet are sized properly now. They were drawn at 2x scale and the kettle was taller than the counter; both render at half size, so a 5-gal stockpot reads as a 5-gal stockpot on a real kitchen counter.

Swipe left/right on the home view to pan the camera across the apartment. The room is wider than the screen, so dragging shows the closet on the far left and the stove + window on the far right. Default camera centers on the sink/kettle.

Closet, stove, and bottling table are tappable now in addition to the kettle. Tapping the stove when nothing's brewing nudges you to start at the kettle; tapping the bottling table previews bottling when something's ready. The tap layer hit-tests against station rects, so pressing-then-dragging pans without firing the tap (8px threshold).
Known: the wall above the counter is mostly empty now that the kettle is the right size. Decor (cabinets, hood, clock) coming as more stations get graphified.
No more landing page. The apartment IS the home screen — kettle on the counter, brass faucet above, stove and bottling table flanking. Open the app and you're already in the kitchen.

All brewing actions are tap-the-world: tap the kettle to start a brew (or resume one mid-flow), tap the closet to check the fermenter or the conditioning rack. The old Start brewing / Check fermenter / Resume brewing buttons are gone.

Status moves to a tiny HUD: day + cash + bottles top-left, Phone / Journal / Rest icons top-right, a floating prompt above the version row tells you what tapping the highlighted object will do (or what's blocking it — "Need ingredients. Tap the phone to shop.").
Changelog scroll left the home view; updates ship via the in-app updater banner instead. The new-build hype is over after rev 70 anyway.
Brewing day takes over the whole screen. The kitchen — sink, counter, stove, bottling table — is the view; no more half-screen sidebar list eating UI space.
Stage progress moved to a small chip in the bottom-left corner ("Step 2 of 7 · Fill kettle" + a one-line hint). Close button is a flat label in the top-right.

Fill kettle no longer has a "Done filling" button or care-factor checkboxes. Turn the faucet off with water in the kettle and the step commits — wiggling the tap on/off counts as careful work and feeds care factor naturally. All brewing progression now happens by interacting with the environment.

Pivot: the apartment is one big room now, not a separate scene per task. Closet on the far left (where the fermenter goes between bottling and tasting), bottling table next to it, kitchen sink with brass faucet, stove with 4 burners + oven door, and a small window with a night sky on the far right. The camera pans to whichever station the active step needs.

Fill kettle now opens at the sink station with the kettle on the counter under the faucet — same brass-handle-tap interaction, same drift math, but you can see the rest of the apartment around it. Other brewing-day steps will pan to their own stations as they get graphified (Pour LME → stove, Cool wort → sink + ice, Transfer + pitch → counter with fermenter, Bottling → table).
Future upgrade scope: when you graduate to garage / pro scale, the room grows new stations rather than being replaced. The apartment IS the world.

Fill Kettle is a real mini-game now — not a form. Apartment kitchen scene with the stockpot on the counter and a brass goose-neck faucet hanging above. Tap the faucet handle to start the water; tap again to stop. Water level rises in real time as the kettle fills.

Eyeballing-from-an-unmarked-stockpot is the load-bearing fiction: a faint gold target band shows roughly where 2½ gallons sits, but the band is wide because you're guessing. Stop too early or too late and your actual_volume drifts; the readout colors green/yellow/orange/red by how close you are.
Pour slowly + Double-check toggles still feed care factor. Tap-stopping the faucet multiple times is also recorded — careful work counts.

Procedurally drawn — palette + lighting from the kept POC, no sprite assets. The shared kitchen scene + procedural kettle + procedural faucet land here as reusable pieces; every other mini-game in the brewing day will graphify against them next.
The other six brewing-day stages still use the form-style placeholders for now. Pour LME is next on the list.

Recipe-driven ingredient prereqs. Start brewing now walks the recipe's fermentables, hop_schedule, and yeast (and adds priming sugar when the recipe uses it) instead of hardcoding APA's specific items. The Need <X> hint pulls the display name from the recipe itself, so when more recipes ship the message reads natural — Need Cascade, Need US-05 dry ale, Need Light Malt Extract — without code changes.

New: Shop app on the phone (Homebrew Supply). Buy ingredients, consumables, and an extra case of bottles. The recipe shopping list totals $51 against your $30 startup capital — you have to skip something. That's the canonical first decision from Appendix A.

Fresh careers now start with empty ingredients (just bottles + dish soap + sponge from the previous life). Start brewing greys out with Need malt extract / Need hops / Need yeast hints until you've shopped. Existing in-progress saves keep whatever ingredients they already had.
After-purchase live readout shows what you'll have left ($30 - $27 = $3) or how short you are. Buy is disabled until your selection is affordable.
v1 stops short of consumption — one purchase carries arbitrarily many brews until the inventory-deplete pass lands. The 'running low on bottles' soft cue from the design is also a separate followup.

Fixed: bottling didn't check whether you actually had bottles. You could complete a 1st brew → leave it in conditioning → finish a 2nd brew → tap Bottle this brew with 0 free bottles, and the 2nd brew silently advanced to conditioning anyway. Now Bottle this brew is disabled in the Check fermenter modal until you have 24 free bottles, with a hint that says to taste a conditioning brew first to free them up.
If you somehow get past the modal (direct route-in, future affordances), the bottling scene's Confirm hard-aborts back to the dashboard rather than transitioning the brew.
New: phone overlay. Tap Phone on the dashboard's bottom row to open it. App grid shows Messages (real), Shop / Forum / News / Calendar (placeholder, coming soon).

Messages opens straight to the Marcus thread — the cold open from Appendix A. Five messages: party invite, the $30 startup capital your folks will chip in, and a torn-page-from-BREW-MAGAZINE attachment. Tap Open recipe → recipe card spread for Apartment Pale Ale.
Phone uses the ModalLayer-style pause: while the overlay is up, brewing-day timers and rest don't tick.
Shop app is the next thing — once it ships, the pre-seeded ingredients go away and Marcus's $30 + the recipe's $39 shopping list become the real first-decision moment.

Fixed: hitting Close mid-brew left a Today checklist row reading brewing_day with no way to interact with it. Now closing the brewing-day scene leaves a Resume brewing — Apartment Pale Ale row in gold; tap it to re-open the scene at the first stage you hadn't finished yet.

Fixed: you could stack two brewing-day brews by hitting Start brewing again. Start brewing is now disabled with a You're already brewing — finish or close that batch first hint until the in-progress brew is resolved.

Fixed: finishing a brewing day didn't refresh the dashboard until you tapped Get some rest. Brewing day now notifies the dashboard the moment you finish (or close), so the Today list updates immediately.

Dashboard restructure: the Brews-in-flight panel is gone, replaced by a Today daily checklist + a morning summary line tied to the day's mood (first day, quiet morning, closet hum, something ready, etc).

Each fermenting / conditioning brew shows up as one checklist row — Check fermenter — Apartment Pale Ale, day 3/5. A ▶ in gold marks the row as actionable when the brew has reached its bottle / taste beat.

Tap a row → Check fermenter modal pops up over a dimmed backdrop. The modal shows the stage + day-N-of-M and a vague airlock observation that shifts as the brew moves through fermentation. The Bottle this brew / Pour & taste action moved off the dashboard row and into this modal.
Modal layer wired to Main: push_modal pauses the rest of the tree, pop_modal unpauses; the modal itself runs with PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS so its buttons still work.

New: brewery journal viewer. Tap View brewery journal on the dashboard to see every brew you've completed, newest first. Each card shows the recipe, the day you finished it, and the colored self / style grades plus the actual OG / FG / IBU / ABV / carbonation you hit.
Empty-state screen explains what to do if you haven't tasted anything yet.

Bottling and tasting are in. Once a brew hits its fermentation days the dashboard surfaces a Bottle this brew button on its row; tap it to open the bottling scene (priming sugar choice, fill method, sanitation toggles). Confirm bottles your batch, flips the brew to conditioning, frees the fermenter, and shifts the 24 bottles into in_use.

After conditioning days have elapsed, the row shows Pour & taste. The tasting scene reveals your actual OG / FG / IBU / ABV / carbonation, computes a self grade against your recipe targets and an external grade against the BJCP-style profile, then logs the whole brew (outcomes + grades + risk profile) to the journal file.

The full pipeline plays end to end now: start brewing → walk all seven brewing-day stages → fermenting (5 days of rest) → bottle → conditioning (14 days of rest) → pour & taste → brew logged, fermenter free, ready for the next batch.

Grades currently cap at C for fresh-career skills (per the design's skill ceiling). Mastering the relevant skills lifts the cap. Final grade colors green at A/A+, yellow at A-/B, gold at C, orange at D, red at F.
Dashboard now shows Brews in flight — each brew lists its name, stage (fermenting / conditioning), and day-N-of-M progress so you can see what's actually happening after the brewing day ends.

Get-some-rest now actually ticks the brew forward. Each rest tap increments fermenting and conditioning brews' days_elapsed; when a brew hits its target days, the line turns green and reads ready to bottle (or ready to drink). Bottling itself isn't a real action yet — that lands once the bottling-day flow ships — but at least the path forward is visible instead of looking stuck.
Brewing-day brews don't accrue days because the player is in the active scene during them (per the design's two-clocks rule).

New mini-game: Boil with hops. Set the burner heat (HIGH/MED/LOW), choose whether to watch for hot break and drop hops on schedule, react to a boil-over the way you'd actually react in the kitchen (lower heat / blow / skim / ignore), and remember the flameout. Each choice tweaks the IBU factor, volume loss, and risk deltas.

All seven brewing-day stages except the "heat" warmup now have real mini-games. The full apartment-pale-ale flow plays end-to-end: sanitize → fill kettle → (heat placeholder) → add LME → boil with hops → cool the wort → transfer + pitch. The brew flips to fermenting and you're back on the dashboard.

Boil's UI is form-style for now. The intended end-state is a real-time mini-game with hop-drop prompts, hot-break recognition, and a boil-over reaction window — that lands once the kitchen render-pipeline art is in. The math contract stays the same; only the input affordance changes.

New mini-game: Transfer + pitch yeast (the final brewing-day stage). Pick your pour quality (gentle vs splashy → oxidation risk) and your pitch method (sprinkle on top or rehydrate first → more process XP). Optional toggles for an even sprinkle, stir-before-pitch, and sanitized funnel each tighten care and remove specific risk lines.

New mini-game: Cool the wort. Pick ice bath (slower, lands ~70°F) or top-off cooling (faster, ~80°F, but the cold water is a sanitation gamble unless you boil it first or use bottled). Each path has its own optional sub-actions; the readout previews your projected final temp and care factor as you pick.

New mini-game: Sanitize fermenter & tools. Pick which steps to take — rinse, soap-wash, Star San, drip-dry. The breadth of actions sets your care factor; the strongest action sets the bucket's persistent state (USED → SERVICEABLE → CLEAN → SANITIZED), which carries forward as the next brew's infection-risk baseline.

Star San is shown but greyed out with a (need to buy) tag because the canonical Appendix A starter inventory skips it. Once the phone shop ships you'll be able to buy it during the cold open. Until then the best you can hit is CLEAN.

New mini-game: Pour LME (the Add malt extract stage). The order matters — turn burner OFF, start stirring, THEN pour. Get it wrong and you'll scorch the kettle. Watch for the colored result line for 1.5 seconds before the stage advances so you can see what happened.
Optional toggles (Read recipe aloud, Pre-warm LME tin) raise your care factor without changing the procedure.

Added a dev Reset save button at the bottom of the dashboard. Use it if your save lands in a stuck state — e.g. a brew stranded in fermenting because the bottling flow doesn't ship yet — and you want to drop back to Day 0 with the starter setup. Removed before launch.

Fixed: the day counter resets to Day 0 every relaunch instead of remembering how many days you've slept through. The day clock now rides in the save file and gets restored on load. (Older saves that predate this field default to Day 0 — only the next session forward will start tracking.)

Fixed: Start brewing showed Recipe not unlocked at first launch and only unlocked after a Get-some-rest tap. The bootstrap reseed was running, but the dashboard had already rendered against the pre-reseed state because the state-loaded signal fired too early.
Fixed: tapping Start brewing on the dashboard appeared to do nothing. The brewing-day scene mounts onto a CanvasLayer now, so it actually draws on top of the dashboard.

Fill Kettle is back, rebuilt against the new outcome model. Pick a water source (tap or bottled jug), pick a method (faucet, funnel, 1L pitcher, or marked jug — each with different precision), optionally pour slowly or double-check the volume for a higher care factor.

Pouring rolls a real volume drift against your Process skill, the method's precision, and your care, and writes the result to the brew's outcomes. Lower-skill / lower-precision pours scatter wider; jug-pours land near-exact.
Stages other than Fill kettle still use the placeholder Continue button — they get their real mini-games in upcoming builds.
Dashboard now has a Start brewing button. Tap it to load the brewing-day scene with the Apartment Pale Ale recipe (the only style v1 ships with).

The brewing-day scene shows the seven stages of the brew (Sanitize · Fill kettle · Heat · Add LME · Boil with hops · Cool · Transfer + pitch) in a sidebar; each stage currently advances on a placeholder Continue button until the real mini-games land in the next builds.

Career bootstrap — fresh saves now include the Appendix A starter equipment (stove, stockpot, bucket fermenter, spoon, thermometer, capper, pitcher, funnel) and enough ingredients to brew the starter recipe. Existing in-progress saves migrate forward.
Save format bumped to v2 to carry the bootstrap. Cash, skills, and any in-flight brews are preserved across the migration.
Architecture rebuild against the locked design spec (DESIGN.md Sections 7 + 8). Foundation lands; brewing flow comes back in subsequent commits.
New autoloads: TimeService (the two clocks — day + scene), GameState (the persistent player tree), SaveService (atomic JSON main + JSONL journal).
New scene graph: persistent Dashboard background, ActiveSceneContainer for mini-games, Phone + Modal CanvasLayers above gameplay.
Sim engine pure-data layer: Drift, Grader, RiskProfile, SkillXP, CareFactor, BrewState, CalendarSurface — ready for mini-games to consume.
The previous brew flow + fill-kettle mini-game were proof-of-concept; they're removed and will be reimplemented against the new contract.

Brewing flow! "Start a new brew" on the home screen now walks through nine stages — measure water, mash, boil, cool, pitch, ferment, bottle, condition, taste — with the kettle mini-game for the first one and "Continue" placeholders for the others.
Each completed stage shows its grade in the stage list. Final grade screen with computed OG / IBU / ABV / volume from the recipe target.
Recipe: Basic Pale Ale (target 4.0 L, ~5% ABV, IBU 35). More recipes land later as progression.

Home-screen equipment icons are now all procedural: stove (with burner + red knobs), kettle (side-view), mash paddle, hydrometer (amber wort sample), beer bottle (gold cap + label). Same palette + lighting as the in-game kettle.
Steam rises from the kettle when there's water in it. Soft cream puffs that grow and fade as they drift upward.
Visual polish pass — single global palette + light direction across every procedural-drawn surface, brass faucet (was gray), kettle with proper lit/shadow sides and a counter shadow.
Post-process layer on the kettle mini-game: vignette, warm color grade, soft bloom on bright highlights, subtle film grain.
Replaced the top-down pot icon on the home screen with a side-view procedural kettle that matches the in-game style.

First mini-game: Fill the kettle. Hold POUR to open the faucet, watch the water rise, tap DONE when the level matches the 4.00 L target. Grade is A+ to F based on accuracy; overflowing the kettle ends the round.
Side-view brew kettle drawn procedurally — hammered-metal body, D-handles, rivets, animated water surface with meniscus, splashes where the stream hits the water.
Side gauge with target band so you can see how close you are without watching the readout.
Reachable via the new "Start brewing — fill the kettle" button on the home screen.
Tapping the update notification now installs the new build in-place — no more browser detour.
Home screen now shows a starter brewing kit grid: stove, pot, mash paddle, hydrometer, hops, malt, yeast, and a finished bottle.
Three new sprites: yeast packet, mash paddle, hydrometer.

Fixed the FCM + in-app updater pipeline: a bad type annotation in the export plugin was silently disabling everything in the APK (no notifications, Update button did nothing). Plugin loads cleanly now.
Push notifications: now actually prompts for the Android notification permission on first launch (was silently dropped on Android 13+).
Fixed the build number on the home screen — was always reading 0.
In-app install: tap Update on the home banner and the new build downloads inside the app, then prompts to install — no browser detour.
Push notifications: when a new build ships you'll now get an Android notification, tap it to grab the APK.
Switched the Android build to Godot's gradle pipeline so we can layer in custom Java; CI verifies the APK is still signed with the same key as previous releases.
In-app updater: home screen now shows an Update banner when a newer build is on GitHub.
Tapping Update opens the release page in your browser to download the APK.
First sprite art lands: an amber beer bottle on the home screen.
AI sprite pipeline online — pixel-art SDXL workflow generating equipment + ingredient sprites.
Migrated from Jetpack Compose to Godot 4.3
New project structure: godot/ project + headless screenshot harness + GUT tests
Phase 1 bootstrap: launches to a Hello Homebrewer screen with version + changelog
FCM update push paused until Phase 2 (Android Custom Build template)
